yavamadhya
(‘the middle of a wheat grain’)
------------------------------------------
See CĀNDRĀYAṆA.

yavanas
------------------------------------------
The word yavana or yona in the epics and the पुराणस् generally stands for foreigners, especially the Greeks and the Muslims. They are described as barbarous people (vide महाभारत, Vanaparva,

) who will rule in कलियुग.
Originally, perhaps, the word might have indicated the Ionians or ancient Greeks.
According to the Rāmāyaṇa (Bāla-kāṇḍa 55) the यवनस् were produced from the hind part of the celestial cow Nandinī to fight against the army of विश्वामित्र.
The Mahābhārata in another place (Ādiparva 85.34) states that the यवनस् sprang from Turvasu, one of the sons of the king ययाति.
The Matsyapurāṇa (114.11) considers the country of the यवनस् as a part of भारतवर्ष.
